questions.question: What is the meaning of 'al-hashr' from which this surah takes its name?
options: A type of armed battle unique to tribal Arabia
The gathering or exile, referring to the expulsion of Banu Nadir from Medina
A term for the distribution of war spoils among fighters
A Medinan term for a binding treaty between tribes
questions.explanation: The word 'al-hashr' means a gathering or exile. Ibn Abbas called this surah 'Surat Bani Nadir' because its central narrative concerns the expulsion of that Jewish tribe from Medina. Verse 2 describes their departure as 'the first gathering,' with Ibn Kathir specifying their destination was Khaybar and Syria.

questions.question: True or false: The Banu Nadir were expelled only after a prolonged military battle in which the Muslims deployed cavalry and suffered significant losses.
questions.explanation: The Banu Nadir were expelled without conventional battle. Allah cast terror into their hearts and they accepted exile. Verse 6 explicitly states no horses or camels were deployed in military engagement, which is precisely why the property obtained was classified as fay rather than ghanimah under Islamic law.

questions.question: Which hadith collection does Ibn Kathir cite when explaining that the Prophet was 'given victory through terror cast into the hearts of enemies at a month's journey'?
options: Sahih Muslim only
Sahih al-Bukhari
Sunan al-Tirmidhi
Musnad of Imam Ahmad
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir, in explaining the phrase 'cast terror into their hearts' from verse 2, cites the well-known hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari in which the Prophet says he was given victory through terror placed in the hearts of his enemies at a distance of a month's journey, connecting this prophetic privilege to the supernatural fear that overcame Banu Nadir despite their fortifications.

questions.question: What is the key distinction between fay and ghanimah that verse 6 establishes?
options: Fay is distributed only among the Muhajireen while ghanimah goes to all Muslims
Fay is wealth obtained without armed combat and belongs to the Prophet to distribute, while ghanimah requires actual battle and is divided among fighters
Fay covers only agricultural land while ghanimah covers moveable possessions
The two terms are synonymous and scholars treat them identically in jurisprudence
questions.explanation: As Imam Tabari records, the companion Umar ibn al-Khattab stated that the wealth of Banu Nadir was pure fay given to the Prophet since no cavalry or camelry was deployed against them. Verse 6 establishes that fay is at the disposal of the Prophet and later the Muslim treasury, in contrast to ghanimah which requires military engagement and is distributed with one-fifth reserved and four-fifths going to fighters.

questions.question: How does Imam Tabari explain the meaning of the word 'dawlah' in the phrase 'so that it will not be a perpetual distribution among the rich'?
options: A permanent political dynasty that controls state resources
A revolving cycle, indicating the verse forbids wealth circulating only among the already wealthy
A tax system in which the rich pay more than the poor
A form of charitable endowment that benefits the poor exclusively
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir, drawing on Imam Tabari's analysis, highlights that the word 'dawlah' in this context means a revolving cycle. The verse therefore prohibits wealth from rotating only within circles of the rich. Imam al-Shafi'i treated this verse as the definitive Quranic text on the distribution of fay, and it is cited by contemporary scholars as a Quranic basis against economic oligarchy.

questions.question: True or false: Classical Sunni scholars considered the command 'whatever the Messenger gives you, take it' in verse 7 to apply only to the distribution of fay wealth, not to other religious rulings.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir records that Ibn Masud cited this very verse when a woman challenged his ruling about plucking eyebrows, demonstrating that the companions understood the command as absolute and universal. Both Tabari and Ibn Kathir affirm this as the foundational Quranic proof for the binding authority of the Sunnah across all areas of life, not merely wealth distribution.

questions.question: What was the hypocrites' secret promise to Banu Nadir, and how did Allah respond in verse 11?
options: They offered to negotiate a peace settlement, and Allah praised their peacemaking
They pledged military support if Banu Nadir resisted or were fought, and Allah declared them liars through divine testimony
They offered financial compensation to the Muslims, and Allah accepted the gesture as sufficient
They promised to convert to Islam on behalf of Banu Nadir, and Allah exposed this as insincere
questions.explanation: As Imam Tabari records, Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions sent word to Banu Nadir promising to leave with them if expelled and to fight alongside them if attacked, even pledging two thousand additional armed men. Allah responds in verse 11 with the declaration 'Allah bears witness that they are surely liars,' a direct divine refutation issued before the promises could even be tested.

questions.question: True or false: According to Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran, the hypocrites compared to Satan in verse 16 were not merely politically unreliable allies but instruments of a deeper cosmic deception.
questions.explanation: Sayyid Qutb notes that the Quran's choice to liken the hypocrites to Satan rather than merely criticizing them reveals the spiritual depth of their corruption. They were not simply unreliable allies but instruments of a deeper cosmic deception, making verse 16 a timeless warning about the nature of all false alliances rooted in shared opposition to righteousness rather than shared principle.

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli, in Al-Tafsir al-Munir, connects verse 19's warning about forgetting Allah to which modern phenomenon?
options: The rise of social media and digital distraction
A crisis of meaning in which forgetting Allah correlates with confusion about human dignity, purpose, and morality
The decline of mosque attendance in Muslim-majority countries
Economic inequality that distracts the poor from spiritual concerns
questions.explanation: Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir connects verse 19 to the modern crisis of meaning, noting that widespread forgetfulness of Allah correlates historically with confusion about human dignity, purpose, and morality. When people forget they are accountable to a Creator, they become susceptible to every ideology that promises identity without accountability.

questions.question: What is the central spiritual lesson of the mountain parable in verse 21?
options: That the physical world is fragile and mountains will eventually erode
That the Quran possesses such immense weight and dignity that even a massive mountain would tremble and split from it, rebuking the human heart that remains unmoved
That Allah can reshape the natural world at will as a sign for disbelievers
That mountains literally glorify Allah and will be witnesses on the Day of Judgment
questions.explanation: The parable contrasts the mountain's hypothetical total submission before the Quran with the human heart that often remains hard and unresponsive. Ibn Kathir explains that Allah highlights the Quran's worth by saying even the most massive earthly creation would be humbled and broken by it. The purpose, as stated in the verse itself, is so that people may reflect, making it a direct rebuke to hearts that hear the Quran without being moved.

questions.question: True or false: Ibn Kathir notes that the names Al-Rahman and Al-Rahim appear at the close of verse 22 in a position that mirrors their placement in Surah Al-Fatiha, signaling that mercy is a central defining attribute of Allah.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir draws attention to the placement of Al-Rahman and Al-Rahim at the close of verse 22, noting that this mirrors their position in Surah Al-Fatiha, the opening chapter of the Quran. He observes this parallel signals that mercy is not an incidental attribute of Allah but a central and defining one, especially striking given that this surah deals with the expulsion of a treacherous tribe.

questions.question: What do the three names Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari, and Al-Musawwir in verse 24 collectively describe, according to Imam Tabari and Ibn Kathir?
options: Three separate moments of divine judgment applied to different categories of humanity
The complete creative process from bringing things into existence, to distinguishing created types, to conferring their unique shapes and forms
Allah's three responses to human sin: creation, warning, and punishment
Three names that are entirely synonymous and serve only as rhetorical emphasis
questions.explanation: Imam Tabari's Jami al-Bayan provides detailed lexical analysis: Al-Khaliq refers to creating from non-existence, Al-Bari to distinguishing and differentiating creation into its distinct natures and species, and Al-Musawwir to conferring the specific forms, shapes, and appearances of each created thing. Together they describe the full scope of divine creative power from concept to finished form.
